title: Check a Kohler KT725 lawn tractor engine's oil with its dipstick, wiping and re-reading it, and mark the level
instruction: Check the oil level on the engine with the dipstick, mark it on the check card with the puck, then put everything back.
context: Checking the oil before mowing is the first maintenance step in a lawn tractor's manual, and owners do it themselves: 63% of US adults own outdoor power equipment (OPEI/Harris Poll 2018). The rig is the low-cost real build: a Kohler KT725's genuine dipstick and fill tube over a quart can of oil, at the corner of a black plywood box in the place of the blower housing, placed as on the engine by Kohler's service manual 32 690 03 Rev. H (drawing p.5; p.42 names lawn tractors). Its procedure (p.41): "Remove dipstick; wipe oil off. Reinsert dipstick into tube; press completely down. Remove dipstick; check oil level. Level should be at top of indicator on dipstick." The first pull is never read: oil splashed up the tube coats the blade above the true level. The level read (ADD, OK or OVER) decides what comes next: add oil, mow, or drain an overfill.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. The rig is the low-cost real build, sized from the p.5 drawing of Kohler's service manual 32 690 03 Rev. H for the KT725 engine and turned so the drawing's oil-filter side faces the robot. An unpainted plywood base 47 x 50 x 0.8 cm is fixed on the table at x 27.7 to 74.7, y -18.8 to 31.2. On it stands a box of 12 mm plywood painted plain black in the place of the engine's blower housing: 41 x 41 cm (x 30.7 to 71.7, y -14.5 to 26.5), 30 cm tall, closed on top (z 30.8). Its near right corner is cut off as two flat faces 15.2 cm wide, from 20 cm along the front and right sides to a point 6 cm in from both, running from the top down to 20 cm above the base and open below; its other three corners are cut at 45 degrees, 13 cm along each side (12 cm at the far right). In that open corner a 1 quart unlined steel paint can (10.8 cm across, 12.4 cm tall) stands on the base under the tube. The black oil fill tube (Kohler 32 123 14-S) 2.1 cm across goes down through the can's lid and rises straight up, 3.5 cm in front of the corner faces and held to one by a steel tab, to a 3.6 cm collar whose top (the mouth) is at x 36, y -12, z 28.3 (27.5 cm above the base, the engine's height from the drawing). The dipstick (Kohler 32 038 14-S) sits seated in it: a steel blade 1.0 x 0.3 x 24.5 cm (its tip 3 cm above the base, in the can's oil) with black ADD and FULL marks 0.8 and 2.0 cm from the tip and a crosshatch between them, its flat faces toward and away from the robot; a yellow ribbed cap 3.2 cm across and 1 cm thick on the collar; a yellow T-handle 3.5 cm wide, 1.8 cm thick and 3.5 cm tall on top (to z 32.8); 29 cm overall, 50 g. It slides only along the tube's axis, and its weight takes it back down onto its seat if let go. The blade's lower 6 cm carries an amber smear of oil (drawn), the false first reading. The true level changes from trial to trial and shows on the blade only after a wipe and a full reseat: 0.4 cm from the tip (below ADD), 1.4 cm (between the marks) or 2.7 cm (above FULL), each 4 mm or more from a mark. A folded blue shop rag, a pad 4 x 4 x 2.5 cm of 40 g, lies loose at x 20, y 0. An oil check card, a dark gray tray 6 x 16 x 1 cm, is fixed at x 20, y 13, with three pockets 4.4 cm square and 5 mm deep at y 18.2 (ADD, amber floor, white minus sign), y 13 (OK, green, check mark) and y 7.8 (OVER, red, plus sign). A white marker puck, 3 cm across, 2 cm tall and 15 g, stands loose at x 14, y 22. Both arms start at their home poses.
scoring: q is the dipstick cap's height above its seat. Out: q at least the blade length plus 5 mm. Seated: q of 3 mm or less. Held: both fingers of a gripper touching the yellow T-handle with their opening stopped by it (across its 1.8 cm thickness or 3.5 cm width); an empty fist or open hand does not count. Blade handled: the dipstick is drawn and pushed by its handle only, since the blade carries the oil; a gripper touching the blade (contact with the gripper's own shape) while it is off its seat scores the trial 0. Wipe: the first pull's blade is smeared above the true level. The rag touches the blade when its middle is within 2.7 cm of the blade's axis, its shape within 2 mm of the blade's faces and its extent overlapping the blade out of the mouth. The blade is wiped once the rag's middle has slid, while touching, over 90% (5.4 cm) of the blade's 6 cm oiled length (the tip up past the highest level, 2.7 cm, and the splash) in that pull; slides count only between two touching steps and at most 5 mm a step, so dabs, a spot wipe or a part stroke do not count. Strokes in one pull add up; the tip going back into the tube clears the count. Reseat: the wiped blade pushed in by the handle until seated; a part-way push that comes out again smears the blade again, and a drop or a seat without a wipe restarts the procedure. Reading: after the reseat, the dipstick pulled out again and held by the handle, out and still (under 1 cm/s), for 1 s. Report: the robot marks the level it read by leaving the puck in the ADD, OK or OVER pocket: its middle within 1.2 cm of the pocket's middle and its bottom 2 mm or more below the card's top, at rest and let go (no gripper touching it, by contact with the gripper's own shape) at the end. A puck in any pocket for 2 steps before the reading is a guess. Scores: doing nothing scores 0. 0 for a handled blade, a wrong report or a guess, whatever else was done, so guessing never pays; 0 if the blade was never wiped and pushed back in until the cap seats. 0.25: wiped and seated by hand, no true reading. 0.5: true reading, no report. 0.75: the right report, but the dipstick not seated by hand and let go, or the rag not put down (at rest, its bottom 1 cm or less above the table, let go). 1.0: all of it. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Always guessing one pocket averages about 0.33 over the three levels, below the 0.5 for reading without reporting. A real trial is scored from the video: the handle-only grip, the rag drawn along at least 5.4 cm of the lower 6 cm, the gap under the cap after each push, the 1 s hold, the frame the puck goes in and the pocket it ends in, and the rag back on the table.
reset_notes: Seat the dipstick and put the rag back at x 20, y 0 and the puck at x 14, y 22. Real rig: the low-cost build the sim models (README, Real-world build); room 20-24 degrees C. Before each trial fit fresh covers (a GloveWorks HD 8 mil nitrile glove over each gripper finger) and a fresh shop towel; the rig stands in a Lisle 19722 drip pan with folded shop towels under the tube, rag and card; used covers and towels go in a lidded 1 gallon metal paint can (BEHR 96601) as the oily waste can after the trial. Reset between trials takes about 8 minutes. Real trials run in blocks of three, one per level in a die-shuffled order. Before each, set the level with a syringe of oil (just under the indicator, mid-range, or just over it) and check it with a pull and wipe; smear oil on the blade's lower 6 cm and up the tube. After each, the tester pulls, wipes, reseats and pulls again and measures the oil band from the tip with a steel rule (mm), and records the set level, the measured band, whether the tip went back into the tube unaided at each push, the pocket the puck is in and the score (README, Results). In the sim OIL_CASE=low, ok or over sets the level; seeded resets pick it; with no jitter it is between the marks.
fidelity: Sim models the low-cost real build (Build B): genuine Kohler dipstick and fill tube at the KT725's mouth height and corner, over a quart can, at the cut-corner black plywood box; a used engine (Build A) gives the same tube and handle. Tube straight (real one bends under the cap). Stick guided on the tube's axis when out; real trials test reinsertion. Stick 29 cm, marks 0.8 and 2.0 cm up; real ones recorded. Oil drawn from scorer state; rag a rigid pad. Gripper covers and drip pan real-only.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 (853 steps). Both on task.py efa506001ca6.
